messages:
Helen (Support): Hey @Mike, getting an escalation from an enterprise customer (org: org_9482) — their daily usage chart for 2026-03-10 is showing spikes that actually happened after midnight (2026-03-11). Screenshot: https://uploads.redwood/esc/9482-chart.png

Mike (Customer Success): ack. Can you paste the org id + a sample CSV export?

Helen (Support): org_9482. CSV export attached: https://files.redwood/exports/org_9482_usage_2026-03-10.csv
The CSV header has timestamps in UTC but the console header says 'Timezone: Australia/Sydney'. Rows around midnight look like 2026-03-11T00:12:00Z but appear under 2026-03-10 in the chart.

metrics-bot: daily-aggregator job delta-run failed for job_id=agg_daily_2026-03-10 at 2026-03-11T13:04:00Z; retry succeeded.

Jia (eng-metrics): assigning to eng-metrics. Quick q: is this only for orgs in DST zones? Any reproducible steps?

Helen (Support): Repro steps I used:
1) Org timezone set to Australia/Sydney in Console.
2) Console -> Usage -> Export CSV for date 2026-03-10.
3) Observe CSV rows with timestamps 2026-03-11T00:15:00Z showing up under the 2026-03-10 daily chart.

Oscar (eng-data): running a quick query against warehouse to inspect local timestamps:
```
select event_time,
       (event_time AT TIME ZONE 'UTC') AT TIME ZONE 'Australia/Sydney' as local_ts
from usage_events
where org_id='org_9482' and event_time >= '2026-03-09'::timestamptz and event_time < '2026-03-12'::timestamptz
order by event_time limit 10;
```
I can see events with event_time 2026-03-10T13:15:00Z -> local_ts 2026-03-11 00:15:00+11.

Oscar (eng-data): Preliminary root cause: the daily aggregator currently does `date_trunc('day', event_time AT TIME ZONE 'UTC')` and then adds a fixed hour offset pulled from org profile (e.g., +11h). That fails on DST transition days (offset can be +10 or +11), so events get grouped into the wrong calendar day.

Oscar (eng-data): Fix is to do timezone-aware truncation: compute `local_ts = (event_time AT TIME ZONE 'UTC') AT TIME ZONE org_tz` then `date_trunc('day', local_ts)` for grouping. Also change CSV exporter to include ISO timestamps with explicit timezone suffix and add an `export_tz` header so the export and UI labels are consistent.

Jia (eng-metrics): Agreed. Low-risk query change. Plan: patch aggregator, run a targeted backfill for affected dates (2026-03-09 -> 2026-03-12) for orgs with DST zones. Rollout ETA ~2 hours. Who can run the backfill?

Oscar (eng-data): I'll land the patch and run backfill. Will test in staging first, then run prod backfill script for `org_9482` and batch of orgs with Australia/Europe zones. Backfill script will re-aggregate `daily_metrics` rows for the given org list and date range.

Helen (Support): Please also add an immediate UI mitigation: change CSV header from 'Timezone: account local' to 'Timezone: UTC (timestamps are UTC) — local grouping fix pending' so customers aren't misled while we backfill.

Mike (Customer Success): I'll update the customer with status and ETA. Draft message: "Hi — we identified a timezone-handling bug affecting a small set of orgs around DST transitions. We're deploying a fix and will backfill your metrics for Mar 9–12. Expect resolution within ~6 hours. Sorry for the disruption."

Jia (eng-metrics): +1

Helen (Support): thanks team :pray:

Mike (Customer Success): assigning a postmortem to eng-metrics after backfill :memo:

Oscar (eng-data): backfill started at 2026-03-11T15:10:00Z; kicking off re-aggregation for org_9482.

metrics-bot: job agg_backfill_org_9482 progress 10%
metrics-bot: job agg_backfill_org_9482 progress 50%
metrics-bot: job agg_backfill_org_9482 progress 100% completed at 2026-03-11T16:22:00Z

Oscar (eng-data): backfill complete. Verified spot-checks: chart buckets now match CSV local timestamps.

Helen (Support): Customer notified and confirmed charts now show correct day boundaries. Closing out the thread.

Mike (Customer Success): :thumbsup:
